§11.2.9 Stacked Bars and Waterfalls

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

charts-stacked-bars-and-waterfalls · charts types

✅ Normative

A stacked segment's value MUST be the segment's own span — the size it draws between its two boundaries — never the cumulative height at its top edge. A waterfall step follows the same rule on a floating segment: its value is the rise or fall the step itself draws. Each segment series is a column; a printed total is a value of its own.

Writing the running total instead of the segment is the failure this family exists to catch. An estimated segment is read at both boundaries, and its value is the difference.

  • A category whose stack has no segment of one series leaves that cell empty.
  • A printed total above a stack sits in the stack's row, in a last column under an empty header cell (see the chart table's layout in Cover Every Data Point§11.1.1).
  • A waterfall's anchor bars (start and end levels) are categories of their own; their values are levels, not changes.

✅ Sample — global-income-report-2026_p59

Eight regional stacks, four legend series, every segment printing its share: 32 values, copied with their percent marks. The running header is elided.

✅ Sample — credit-outlook-jun2025_p12

Unlabeled segments over a percent grid, with legend-named components and a printed total above each stack. Every segment is read as its own span — EUR High Yield's grey segment runs from about 2.5% to 5.7%, so its value is 3.2%, not 5.7% — and carries the axis's percent mark. Three of the five classes have no hedging segment: those cells are empty. The printed totals, in bold, sit in the last column. The source line runs off the right edge of the page and is written as far as it is visible.

✅ Sample — renewables-outlook-2025_p24

A waterfall between two anchors: 2024 prints its level (10 000), 2030 and the five steps are estimates, each step its own rise. A marker series for each share rides on the anchors against the right-hand axis, printing its values (see Dual-Axis and Combo Charts§11.2.2); the steps have no markers, so those cells are empty. The printed second axis tier (Generation, Change) groups the categories and has a column of its own; Change spans the five steps as printed. The bars have no legend entry, so their column is headed by the left-hand axis title. Estimates are written in the axis's digit grouping.

✅ Sample — a waterfall where every step prints its value

Eight steps from EBT to FCF, each printing its value above or below its bar, negatives in parentheses; Tax paid and Working Capital are drawn as a line rather than a bar and print their values the same way. Every value is copied as printed. The category labels keep their footnote superscripts, and the unit note heads the value column. The page heading above the chart, and the panels and notes below it, are elided.

✅ Sample — stacked bars with an annotation column

Four horizontal stacks, one per business area, each printing a growth figure at its end and, in a column to the right, one or two lines naming sub-businesses with their own growth. This is one table, one row per bar, with a column holding each row's annotation lines as a list, so the annotations stay attached to their bar. The two segments of each stack print no value and no axis calibrates them, so they give no column; their legend follows the table as text. The labels and growth figures in heavier type are bold.
